D018-D013_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for a few months now. I used to be into online gaming and playing pickup basketball, but lately I just can’t make myself care. Even when friends text to hang out, I just ignore it or say I’m tired.

My mind keeps going back to what happened last year. Sometimes it’s like I’m not even in the present anymore. I’ll hear a loud noise, or a car backfire, and suddenly I’m right back there, like it’s actually happening again. My heart just starts pounding and my hands shake, and it takes a long time to calm down, even when I know I’m safe.

I keep replaying it and thinking, “If he hadn’t done that, none of this would’ve happened,” and I get stuck on how it was other people’s fault. The fear I felt then still kind of sits in my chest, like it never really went away.

Day to day stuff feels hard. Even choosing what to wear, or what to eat, I’ll just stare at things, unable to decide. I’m supposed to be applying for jobs, but I put it off and feel kind of empty and stuck.
D018-D013_h001.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
D018-D013_h001.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h002.question:
I guess this really started maybe a few months ago… it’s hard to pin down exactly. I still go to work most days, but I’m not really “there.” I’ll be trimming hedges or using the blower and suddenly it’s like I’m back in that moment from last year when the accident happened on site. For a few seconds I forget I’m in someone’s garden. I can smell it, hear it, like it’s happening again. Then I kind of snap out of it and feel shaky and embarrassed.

Since then I’ve been keeping to myself a lot more. The lads from work ask me out for a drink and I always make some excuse. Even with my family, I don’t really answer calls. I just feel like I’m not much fun to be around, and part of me thinks it was my fault anyway, that I should’ve done something differently that day.

I’m on edge all the time. If someone drops a tool or a car backfires, I jump out of my skin. It’s awkward when a client notices. My mind wanders a lot too; I’ll reread the same text or forget what someone just told me. Most evenings I just sit at home feeling tense and low, but I’m not sure if it’s just stress or something else.
D018-D013_h002.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
D018-D013_h002.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h003.question:
It’s been… I’d say a few months now that things have felt off. Little things make me jump now—if a car backfires outside or the phone rings loudly, I flinch. And I find my mind wandering during conversations; people talk and I lose the thread halfway through.

    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D013_h004.question:

    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D018-D013_h005.question:

    B. Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h006.question:

There was this thing that happened last year—I don’t really want to talk about it in detail. Whenever something reminds me of it, it’s like I’m not in my dorm anymore. I’m back there. I’ll zone out in lecture and suddenly I’m seeing it play out again, like a clip on repeat, and my heart is pounding. Sometimes someone will tap me on the shoulder from behind and I just jump out of my skin. Once I shoved a guy in the hallway for grabbing my arm as a joke, and another time I slammed my desk so hard my phone flew across the room. I’m not usually that kind of person.

I try really hard not to think about what happened—if any thoughts about it start, I shut them down, scroll my phone, go for a run, anything. But it still sneaks in.

Lately I just feel…flat. My parents say they love me on FaceTime and I know I should feel something, but it’s like it doesn’t land. Same with my ex—I know I cared, but now it’s like I’m watching someone else’s life. I don’t really enjoy the stuff I used to, and most days I’m just tired and going through the motions of classes and assignments. I’m not sure if that’s just stress from school or something else, but it’s been hanging around for a while now.

A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h006.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h007.question:
I guess this started… maybe a few months ago? It’s hard to pin down. There’s this thing that happened years back that I don’t really remember clearly. It’s like big chunks of it are just… blank. I avoid talking about that time with anyone; I just say, “I don’t really remember.”

I lose track of where I am for a second.

I’ve also noticed that even when I do well at work—nailing a tricky appraisal, getting good feedback—I can’t feel proud of it. It’s like there’s this flatness. I’ve snapped a couple of times too; once I slammed a loupe so hard it cracked, and another time I shoved a coworker’s hand away more roughly than I meant to. I don’t usually see myself as an angry person, but lately I feel on edge, tired, and sort of disconnected from things I used to enjoy.
D018-D013_h007.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h007.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h008.question:

D018-D013_h009.question:

D018-D013_h010.question:

D018-D013_h011.question:
It’s hard to separate out when this all started exactly, but I’d say it’s been gradually building over the last few months, maybe longer. I just feel…worn down all the time. I still go into work, but I avoid certain cases and meetings if I know they’ll involve situations that remind me of some of the worst files I’ve had. Even driving near certain neighborhoods or passing the courthouse, my chest tightens and I feel flooded, like I’m right back in it, and I have to look away or change my route.

I’ve become really cynical. I catch myself thinking the world is just fundamentally unsafe, especially for kids, and that what I do doesn’t really matter because things are going to go wrong anyway. That bleeds into everything—sometimes I think life in general just doesn’t have a point.

At home I’m more irritable. My husband and even my sister have said I snap over small things—like I’ll suddenly raise my voice, swear, or lash out, then feel guilty afterward. I also keep replaying how certain cases were handled and find myself blaming specific people—colleagues, supervisors, even the system—for how things turned out.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D018-D013_h011.answer: A & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h012.question:
I’ve been out in the woods my whole life, but the last few months something’s off. Ever since that big fire last summer, it’s like part of my head’s stuck back there. Sometimes when I’m walking a line and catch a certain smell of smoke or hear a branch crack, it’s not just a memory—I’m right back in it. For a few seconds I lose track of where I actually am, like I’m seeing and hearing the fire again.

I try not to think about it. If a thought about that day starts to come up, I shut it down, keep busy with paperwork or radio checks. I avoid talking about it with the younger rangers; I just can’t go there.

I’ve also found myself thinking people are basically out for themselves now. I don’t trust the folks who planned that operation—I keep telling myself it was their bad decisions that cost lives, that if they’d listened to us on the ground, things wouldn’t have gone like that.

Little things set me off lately. Someone’s late to a briefing, or a camper ignores a posted sign, and I snap, raise my voice more than the situation deserves. It passes quick, but it’s like this fuse is shorter than it used to be. Along with that, I’ve just felt heavier, kind of worn down and sad most days, even when I’m out in the trees where I usually feel best.
D018-D013_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D018-D013_h012.answer: A & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h013.question:

D018-D013_h014.question:

D018-D013_h015.question:

I keep thinking it was my fault somehow, like if I’d moved faster or said something different, maybe it wouldn’t have been so bad. And then that turns into this whole thing of, “there’s something wrong with me, I’m just not good enough at my job, or as a person.”

I’m also more snappy than I used to be. Tiny things—a coworker being slow, someone bumping me in the aisle—set me off. I’ll raise my voice, then feel stupid and guilty afterward. D018-D013_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h017.question:
